[L3] If $F$ is a continuous symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on a chart domain $U$ and $\int_UF_{ab}q^{ab}w\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth symmetric compactly supported $q$, then $F=0$ on $U$ ([[lem-gr-compact-variation-coefficient-vanishing]], [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; vary the Lagrangian density in the field and in the metric, integrate by parts using the vanishing of compactly supported divergence integrals, and differentiate the stress-energy formula.

2.1 (Integration by parts.) Consider the smooth compactly supported vector field $J^b:=\delta\varphi\,g^{ab}\partial_a\varphi$; by [L1], $
abla_bJ^b=(\partial_b\delta\varphi)g^{ab}\partial_a\varphi+\delta\varphi\,\Box_g\varphi$, and $\int_M
abla_bJ^b\mathrm{vol}_g=0$ by [L2]. Hence $\int_M(g^{ab}\partial_a\varphi)\partial_b\delta\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\int_M\delta\varphi\,\Box_g\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, and step 1.1 gives $ rac{d}{du}\Delta S= rac{K}{c}\int_M(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi))\delta\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, which is the variation formula in (a). Every compactly supported smooth scalar $f$ is an admissible first variation, by $\varphi_u=\varphi+uf$. Let $E=\Box_g\varphi-V\prime(\varphi)$. If all such variations are stationary, positivity of $K/c$ gives $\int Ef\,\mathrm{vol}_g=0$. On any oriented coordinate chart and for every compactly supported symmetric tensor $q$, take $f=g_{ab}q^{ab}$, extended by zero. Then $\int(Eg_{ab})q^{ab}w\,d^4x=0$, so [L5] gives $Eg=0$. Nondegeneracy of $g$ forces $E=0$ at every point. Conversely $E=0$ makes every variation derivative vanish by the displayed formula. This proves all of (a). [step 1.1, L1, L2, L5, algebra]

2.2 (Metric variation.) With $\Psi:=	frac12g^{ab}\partial_a\varphi\partial_b\varphi+V(\varphi)$ so that $\Delta S=- rac{K}{c}\int_M\Psi\mathrm{vol}_g$ along the metric family, differentiate at $s=0$: $\partial_s\Psi=	frac12\partial_a\varphi\partial_b\varphi\,q^{ab}$, and by [L2] $\partial_s\mathrm{vol}_g=-	frac12g_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$. Therefore $$\partial_s igl(\Psi\mathrm{vol}_g igr) ig|_0=	frac12\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\partial_b\varphi-g_{ab}\Psi\Bigr]q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g=	frac{1}{2K}T_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$$ by the definition of $T$ in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] clause (c). Differentiating under the integral by [L4] and multiplying by $-K/c$ gives (b). [step 1.1, L2, L3, L4, algebra]

3.1 (Conservation identity.) By [L1], $
abla^aT_{ab}=K igl[
abla^a(\partial_a\varphi\partial_b\varphi)-
abla_b igl(	frac12\partial^c\varphi\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi) igr) igr]$. The first term is $K[(
abla^a\partial_a\varphi)\partial_b\varphi+\partial_a\varphi
abla^a\partial_b\varphi]=K[\Box_g\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi+\partial_a\varphi
abla_b\partial^a\varphi]$ by torsion freedom, and the second is $K[\partial_a\varphi
abla_b\partial^a\varphi+V'(\varphi)\partial_b\varphi]$. Subtracting gives $
abla^aT_{ab}=K(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi))\partial_b\varphi$, which is the identity in (c). The forward conservation consequence follows by substitution. At a point with $d\varphi
e0$ choose a tangent vector $X$ with $d\varphi(X)
e0$; if conservation holds, evaluating the identity on $X$ and using $K>0$ gives $\Box_g\varphi-V\prime(\varphi)=0$. If such points are dense, smoothness gives the same equation everywhere. For the necessity of this caveat take $\varphi=a$ constant and a smooth potential with $V\prime(a)
e0$: then $T=-KV(a)g$ is conserved by metric compatibility, while the scalar equation fails. This proves all of (c). [step 2.2, L1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Existence is not claimed.** The proposition identifies the equation satisfied by stationary configurations of the action difference; it asserts neither that $\Box_g\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ has solutions on a given $(M,g)$ nor any well-posedness property.

- **Dependence on the sign convention.** Changing the overall sign of $\ell$ reverses the sign of $\Delta S$ and of the Hilbert tensor, and correspondingly the field equation; the proposition is stated for the convention fixed in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]].

[L4] The integral of the exterior derivative of a compactly supported smooth $3$-form on the oriented four-manifold $M$ vanishes; in particular $\int_M\nabla_aJ^a\,\mathrm{vol}_g=0$ for every smooth compactly supported vector field $J$, since $\nabla_aJ^a\mathrm{vol}_g=d(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g)$ and $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ has compact support ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]], [[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (a), [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]).

[L5] If a continuous covector field $W$ on a chart domain satisfies $\int_UW_aq^aw\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth compactly supported vector field $q$ supported in the chart, then $W=0$; and the chart integral of a compactly supported divergence is zero ([[lem-gr-compact-variation-coefficient-vanishing]], [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]).

[L7] For a global flow $\Phi_v$ of $\xi$, the derivative $\partial_v(\Phi_v^*K)|_{v=0}$ is the Lie derivative $\mathcal L_\xi K$ of the tensor field $K$; moreover $(\Phi_v^*g)^{-1}=\Phi_v^*(g^{-1})$ for every $v$ ([[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]).

[L8] If a map $F:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable at $(0,0)$, then $s\mapsto F(s,s)$ is differentiable at $0$ with derivative $\partial_1F(0,0)+\partial_2F(0,0)$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[def-interval]]).
